A FEW WAYS IN

About this experiment

Drag or tap to set the release height. Left/right changes gravity; up/down changes height. Space or the Gravity button cycles Earth, Moon, Mars, Jupiter and zero gravity. R or Drop again repeats the same release. Rebound controls energy lost at impact: 0 does not bounce, 1 bounces forever. Playback speed slows or accelerates time without changing the motion. P pauses; all controls and PNG export still work while paused. With reduced motion the ball starts suspended until you press P.

The mathematics

A ball falls vertically under constant gravity onto a fixed floor. Each flight segment uses the exact constant-acceleration equations; collisions are resolved at their computed impact time. Rebound e is the coefficient of restitution: zero sticks at the floor, one retains the same bounce height, and intermediate values retain e² of the vertical mechanical energy per impact. There is no air resistance or spin, and ball size is illustrative. Release height measures clearance above the floor. Tiny inelastic rebounds below 0.015 m/s settle to rest. Changing gravity, rebound, or release height starts a new drop from rest. Playback speed changes simulated seconds per real second. Approximate Earth, Moon, Mars, Jupiter and zero-gravity presets provide repeatable comparisons; a uniform field is used for every preset.
